title: A sped-up or slowed clip shows its original length beside it
goal: When you change a clip's speed, nothing on the timeline shows how long the clip was before, so you cannot see what the change did. The speed mock draws a Source row with a striped ghost bar at the original length right above the retimed clip, the before and after the user asked to keep. Draw that row for a picked clip whose speed is not 100%.
notes: Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-speed.html ~47 (.srcbar style) and ~375-376 (a 'Source' track row holding .srcbar above the 'Retimed' row). docs/design/video-surface.md ~316: 'video-speed's Source/Retimed pair is the user's before-and-after and stays as drawn', and a row may be 'a track, or a property lane under one'. Build it the way key lanes already open under a picked clip (property lane), labelled Source with the image icon, rather than as a real track in the document: it is a view of the clip, not something you edit. If it cannot fit as a lane (the placement table in docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md has no row for it), open a decision card and block. Out of scope: the speed curve with stops, which video-surface.md section 11 drops on purpose, and the Slow-mo/Normal/Fast legend. The striped look is already used by the empty track slot (7a15b411), so reuse that drawing. Found by the manager pass's mock comparison 2026-10-07; searched source retimed, ghost bar, before and after speed with --all, nothing covered it.
acceptance: Picking a clip whose speed is not 100% shows a Source lane next to it with a dashed, striped bar at the clip's length at 100%, starting where the clip starts, as video-speed.html draws it (16 point bar, 45 degree stripes in the line colour at 60%, dashed strong-line edge)
The lane goes away when the clip is not picked or its speed is set back to 100%, and it never takes a drop or a click meant for the tracks
Changing the speed from the Speed dropdown or Command R resizes the retimed clip while the ghost stays put, so the before and after read at a glance

Try path at Next defaults: open the talk sample, pick it, press Command R and choose 50%, and the Source lane shows the original length. A walk photographs it beside the mock; audit written under queue/audits/
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Adversarial pass before building: the mock puts Source ABOVE Retimed, but a row opening above the picked clip would push the clip down under the pointer at the moment of the click, so it opens under the track like Zoom and key lanes (UX-PATTERNS D18 rule 6). Found in the first build: at 2x the timeline fits the shorter video, so the ghost ran off the right edge and the before/after did not read. Fixed by letting the ruler cover the ghost's end while a retimed clip is picked (same mechanism as drop room); held off during a clip drag so nothing rescales under the hand.

Left rough, no task (does not clear the bar): picking a sped-up last clip widens the timeline on mouse-up and unpicking fits it back; the ghost has no tooltip because it takes no clicks. Both are in the audit for the user to react to. Speed curve and legend stay out per speed-a-stretch-up-slow-a-moment-down.

Picking a clip whose speed is not 100% opens a Source lane under it with the mock's dashed, striped ghost at the clip's 100% length (Sources/Photonz/ClipSourceLane.swift over tested PhotonzCore/ClipSourceGhost.swift); the ruler widens to the ghost's end while a retimed clip is picked. Verified: a-retimed-clip-shows-its-source-walk at Next defaults (6 real captures, dark and light), 10 neighbouring walks green, Scripts/test.sh 11751 tests green. Audit: queue/audits/2026-10-07-retimed-source-ghost.json
